evals.name: maven-both-declarative
evals.prompt: In ./shipments-api, add Dapr pub/sub: publish a ShipmentCreated event (shipmentId, carrier, destination) on a shipments topic when a shipment is created, and handle those events in this app by logging them. Show me the plan first, then go ahead without waiting for my approval.
evals.expected_output: An Add Pub/Sub Plan with declarative as the default subscription type, app port 8083 read from server.port, and question 2 (POST /shipments also publishes) defaulting to yes because no test calls it over HTTP; no dependency-update question. Then targeted edits: the dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1 import and dapr-spring-boot-starter in pom.xml, @EnableConfigurationProperties(DaprPubSubProperties.class) on ShipmentsApplication, the pub/sub properties appended to application.properties, the ShipmentCreated record, handler, TopicEventStatus, ProcessedEvents, a scoped UnreadableEventAdvice, a declarative events controller with plain @PostMapping routes, a POST /pubsub/shipments publish endpoint, ShipmentController publishing after it creates the shipment with publishEvent(...).block(), dapr.yaml (appPort 8083), resources/pubsub.yaml, resiliency.yaml and subscription.yaml scoped to shipments-api, pubsub.http, DAPR-PUBSUB.md; `mvn -q -DskipTests package` after each step and a final `mvn -q test` with the three existing tests passing; README untouched.
expectations: Before the first file change, the response (or transcript) contains an Add Pub/Sub Plan that names the target shipments-api, Spring Boot 4.0.8 with Maven, app port 8083 read from server.port in application.properties, role both, and the line `**Subscription type:** declarative — default`

The plan's Questions section asks whether `POST /shipments` should also publish ShipmentCreated, with yes as the default, and asks no dependency-update question (the project has no Dapr dependency yet)

pom.xml imports io.dapr.spring dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1 (type pom, scope import) in dependencyManagement and adds dapr-spring-boot-starter without a <version>; the parent stays spring-boot-starter-parent 4.0.8, java.version stays 17, and the existing dependencies are unchanged
ShipmentsApplication.java carries @EnableConfigurationProperties(DaprPubSubProperties.class) next to @SpringBootApplication, and no second @SpringBootApplication class exists

src/main/resources/application.properties still starts with the original `spring.application.name=shipments-api` and `server.port=8083` lines, and now also sets `dapr.pubsub.name=pubsub`, the topic `shipments` and the dead-letter topic `shipments-deadletter`; no application.yml is created

A new @RestController has `@PostMapping("/pubsub/shipments")` that publishes with `daprClient.publishEvent(pubSubProperties.getName(), topic, ...).block()`, taking DaprClient and DaprPubSubProperties through its constructor into final fields; no file uses DaprMessagingTemplate or field @Autowired

ShipmentController's POST handler still calls shipments.create(shipment) and returns ResponseEntity.created(...) with the same body, and now also publishes a ShipmentCreated built from the created shipment (its server-generated id as shipmentId) with publishEvent(...).block() after create succeeds; DaprClient is a constructor parameter and final field; the GET handler is unchanged

The subscriber is declarative: a controller with plain `@PostMapping("/events/pubsub/shipments")` and `@PostMapping("/events/pubsub/shipments-deadletter")` methods taking `@RequestBody CloudEvent<...>` and returning `{"status": ...}` through TopicEventStatus, with no @Topic anywhere; a ShipmentCreatedHandler returns DROP for a blank shipmentId and SUCCESS for a duplicate through ProcessedEvents, and only logs the event

UnreadableEventAdvice exists, maps HttpMessageNotReadableException to 200 with DROP, is ordered first with `@Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE)` and is scoped to the new events controller (`@RestControllerAdvice(assignableTypes = ...)`), so a malformed body sent to POST /shipments still answers 400

dapr.yaml is created in shipments-api with one app entry: appID shipments-api, appDirPath ., appPort 8083 and command ["mvn", "spring-boot:run"]; resources/pubsub.yaml (component pubsub), resources/resiliency.yaml (inbound retry for pubsub) and resources/subscription.yaml (kind Subscription, topic shipments, deadLetterTopic shipments-deadletter, plus a dead-letter document, scopes [shipments-api]) exist

README.md is byte-for-byte unchanged, .gitignore keeps its lines and gains `.dapr/`, and DAPR-PUBSUB.md exists in shipments-api with the topics table, how to start (`dapr run -f .`), a curl example on port 8083, the declarative delivery semantics (a dropped message goes to the dead-letter topic) and a Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard section

The transcript shows `mvn -q -DskipTests package` after each apply step and a final `mvn -q test` that passes (ShipmentServiceTest's two tests and ShipmentsApplicationTests.contextLoads, 3 tests, 0 failures) without a running Dapr sidecar; ShipmentService.java, Shipment.java and everything under src/test are unchanged
No git command other than `git status` was run

Dev Dashboard: before changing files the agent runs `diagrid-dev-dashboard --version` once without stopping, and the final output ends with exactly `Dapr pub/sub is added to shipments-api. Open DAPR-PUBSUB.md in the shipments-api folder for what changed and how to run it.` followed only by the matching Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

evals.name: programmatic-existing-topic
evals.prompt: In ./notifications-service, also subscribe to the payments topic: for each PaymentReceived event (paymentId, customerEmail, amount) send the customer a receipt e-mail with the existing EmailSender. Show the plan, then proceed without asking me.
evals.expected_output: A plan that records the existing (pubsub, emails) programmatic subscription and follows its type, reuses the pubsub component and the existing dapr.yaml entry (appPort 8086 kept), adds a @Topic route pair for payments with a dead-letter topic, a handler that deduplicates on paymentId before calling EmailSender, TopicEventStatus, ProcessedEvents and a scoped UnreadableEventAdvice, the topic properties, and components/resiliency.yaml; the emails subscription stays exactly as it was, no subscription.yaml and no second pubsub component are created, and the build and all three existing tests (EmailSenderTest's two and NotificationsApplicationTests.contextLoads) pass.
expectations: Before the first file change, the plan lists the existing subscription (pubsub `pubsub`, topic `emails`, programmatic, EmailEventsController) and its Subscription type line says `programmatic — follows existing @Topic subscriptions`; role subscriber, so it asks no publish question, and it asks no dependency-update question (the project is on dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1)

EmailEventsController.java is byte-for-byte unchanged, and `emails` is subscribed exactly once in the project (one @Topic on ${app.emails-topic}, no Subscription YAML or streaming subscription for it)

A new controller has `@Topic(name = "${app.<...>}", pubsubName = "${dapr.pubsub.name}", deadLetterTopic = "${app.<...>}")` on a POST route for the payments topic and a second @Topic route for the dead-letter topic, both taking `@RequestBody CloudEvent<...>`; the topic names come from properties, not string literals

application.properties keeps its four original lines unchanged and gains the payments topic (`payments`) and dead-letter topic (`payments-deadletter`) keys, named in the same style as the existing `app.emails-topic` key (for example `app.payments-topic` and `app.payments-dead-letter-topic`)

A PaymentReceived record and a PaymentReceivedHandler exist; the handler returns DROP for a blank paymentId, checks ProcessedEvents before calling the existing EmailSender.send(...) for the receipt, marks the id processed after the send, and lets an exception from EmailSender propagate so Dapr retries

UnreadableEventAdvice exists, maps HttpMessageNotReadableException to 200 with DROP, is ordered first with `@Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE)` and is scoped to the new payments events controller with `assignableTypes`

The plan says the existing EmailEventsController (emails) stays outside the scoped advice and still answers 400 to an unreadable event, and that the new components/resiliency.yaml targets the `pubsub` component, so its retries also apply to the existing emails subscription; DAPR-PUBSUB.md says the same

No `kind: Subscription` YAML is created, components/pubsub.yaml is unchanged and is the only `type: pubsub.` component, no resources/ folder is created, and components/resiliency.yaml is added with an inbound retry for the `pubsub` component
dapr.yaml is byte-for-byte unchanged (the notifications-service entry already has appPort 8086), and the pom.xml is byte-for-byte unchanged (the starter and the 1.19.1 BOM are already there)
The transcript shows `mvn -q -DskipTests package` succeeding after the code steps and a final `mvn -q test` passing (EmailSenderTest's two tests and NotificationsApplicationTests.contextLoads)

DAPR-PUBSUB.md exists with both topics in its Topics table (emails, existing; payments, new) and says programmatic subscriptions are read at sidecar start, so the app and sidecar need a restart after a change
No git command other than `git status` was run

evals.name: maven-streaming
evals.prompt: In ./shipments-service, add Dapr pub/sub: publish a ShipmentCreated event (shipmentId, carrier, destination) on a shipments topic when a shipment is created, and consume those events in this app with a streaming subscription that logs them. Show the plan, then proceed.
evals.expected_output: An Add Pub/Sub Plan with streaming as the requested type, stating that the streaming API acks every event so the handler cannot choose RETRY or DROP, and a dependency-update question (dapr-spring-bom 1.18.1 → 1.19.1, dapr-spring-boot-4-starter → dapr-spring-boot-starter, default yes); then pom.xml on dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1 with dapr-spring-boot-starter, a StreamingConfiguration with a `@Bean(defaultCandidate = false)` DaprPreviewClient, a SmartLifecycle streaming subscriber whose consumer catches RuntimeException inside doOnNext and whose streams have retryWhen, no UnreadableEventAdvice, no subscription.yaml and no subscription routes, dapr.yaml keeping appPort 8083 because the app still serves HTTP, ShipmentController publishing after create, TrackingService unchanged, and a passing `mvn -q test`.
expectations: The plan's Subscription type line says `streaming` (requested), and the plan states that the streaming API acknowledges every event it hands to the app, so the handler cannot choose RETRY or DROP

Before the first file change the plan says a newer Dapr version is available and asks question 1 about the dependency update (dapr-spring-bom 1.18.1 → 1.19.1, with dapr-spring-boot-4-starter replaced by dapr-spring-boot-starter because 1.19 has no separate Boot 4 starter), with yes as the default; the publish question for `POST /shipments` is question 2

pom.xml imports io.dapr.spring dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1 (type pom, scope import) and depends on dapr-spring-boot-starter without a <version>; no dapr-spring-boot-4-starter and no second Dapr BOM remain, the parent stays spring-boot-starter-parent 4.0.8, java.version stays 17, and the other dependencies are unchanged

A @Configuration class declares the DaprPreviewClient as `@Bean(defaultCandidate = false)` built with `daprClientBuilder.buildPreviewClient()` from the injected DaprClientBuilder, and the streaming subscriber takes it as `@Qualifier("daprPreviewClient") DaprPreviewClient` (the app also injects DaprClient, in ShipmentController and as `DaprClient client` in the existing TrackingService, and both beans are DaprClientImpl, which implements both interfaces)

A @Component implementing SmartLifecycle calls `previewClient.subscribeToTopic(...)` for the shipments topic with the dead-letter topic and for the dead-letter topic, each stream with `.retryWhen(Retry.backoff(...)...transientErrors(true))` before `.subscribe()`; the topic consumer wraps the handler call in try/catch (RuntimeException e) that logs; the Disposables are kept and disposed in stop()
No `kind: Subscription` YAML, no @Topic, no `/events/pubsub/shipments` route and no UnreadableEventAdvice are created
dapr.yaml has the shipments-service entry with appPort 8083 kept (the app still serves its HTTP API), and resources/pubsub.yaml and resources/resiliency.yaml exist
ShipmentController's POST handler still calls shipments.create(shipment) and returns its original response, and now also publishes ShipmentCreated with publishEvent(...).block() after create succeeds

The transcript shows a final `mvn -q test` passing 3 tests without a sidecar (the streaming subscription keeps retrying in the background; ShipmentsApplicationTests.contextLoads starts with both the preview client bean and the existing TrackingService(DaprClient client), which fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException without `defaultCandidate = false`), and TrackingService.java and every file under src/test are unchanged
DAPR-PUBSUB.md states the streaming delivery semantics: the app cannot choose RETRY or DROP, a failed handler loses the event, and only a body that cannot be deserialized is dead-lettered
No git command other than `git status` was run

evals.name: spring-security-risk
evals.prompt: In ./returns-api, add Dapr pub/sub: publish a ReturnRequested event (returnId, orderId, reason) on a returns topic when a return is requested, and handle those events in this app by logging them.
evals.expected_output: An Add Pub/Sub Plan and a request for approval; no file in returns-api is changed. The plan reads app port 8089 from server.port in application.yml, picks declarative (default), and because the app uses Spring Security (spring-boot-starter-security and the SecurityFilterChain in SecurityConfiguration) carries a Risk line naming /dapr/subscribe, /dapr/config and /events/pubsub/** as routes the sidecar calls that need a login and a CSRF token, with Dapr's APP_API_TOKEN (dapr-api-token header) as the safer option, plus a question offering DaprSecurityConfiguration with no as the default. SecurityConfiguration stays unchanged.
expectations: The response contains an Add Pub/Sub Plan naming the target returns-api, Spring Boot 4.0.8 with Maven, app port 8089 read from server.port in src/main/resources/application.yml, role both and `**Subscription type:** declarative — default`, and ends by asking the user to approve, change or stop

The plan has a Risk line saying the app uses Spring Security (spring-boot-starter-security and/or the SecurityFilterChain in SecurityConfiguration), that the routes the Dapr sidecar calls (/dapr/subscribe, /dapr/config and /events/pubsub/** or the new event routes) need a login and POSTs a CSRF token, that deliveries would then get 401 or 403 and be retried and dead-lettered, and that Dapr's app API token (APP_API_TOKEN, sent as the dapr-api-token header) is the safer option

The Questions section offers adding a SecurityFilterChain (for example DaprSecurityConfiguration) that lets only the sidecar's routes through without a login or CSRF, with no as the default; it also asks whether `POST /returns` should publish ReturnRequested (default yes) and asks no dependency-update question

The plan does not list SecurityConfiguration.java, application.yml or the spring-boot-starter-security dependency among the edited files; application.yml is the properties file it will append the pub/sub keys to (no application.properties is planned)
No file in the returns-api fixture is added, changed or deleted (hash check), and no `mvn` command or file write was run on the fixture
